note.question: How should joint assortment be designed for an omni-channel retailer?
note.overview: With the growing popularity of e-commerce, nearly every prominent retailer is aiming to turn omni-channel. One crucial decision in this pursuit is the identification of the joint assortment. In this study, we contribute by examining joint assortment and product prices for a retailer that sells products through both brick-and-mortar and online channels.

components.label: Multiple Customer Classes
components.explanation: The model is difficult to examine analytically, so the results in this section are obtained computationally using a dynamic program. (The program and associated details are available in Section EC.17 in the online appendix.) Using the program, we conduct a sensitivity analysis with respect to six parameters, As,s,λs,λw,λo,G and δ, for both uniformly and triangular distributed customer preferences. (Sample assortments are available in Tables EC.8 and EC.9 in the online appendix for different values of λs and λw when customer preferences are triangular distributed and in Table EC.10 of the online appendix for different values of G when customer preferences are uniformly distributed.) The experiments indicate that many insights from Sections 3 and 4 continue to hold.
